claude_code.verification_method: changelog + live-CLI method (automated nightly review). This entry had drifted: master's own copy stayed pinned at 2.1.263 (verified 2026-09-06/07) while the review work for 2.1.267 through 2.1.272 accumulated on this repo's long-open rolling `claude-code-update` PR without ever landing. The 2.1.263→2.1.273 reconciliation cycle (2026-09-16) merged that PR against current master and extended coverage to 2.1.273 on changelog evidence only, no live CLI being available then. The 2026-09-17 cycle had a live `claude` CLI in the automation environment, reporting exactly `2.1.274` — the current release at that time — so `validated_against` advanced all the way to it on real evidence, and `claude plugin validate .` was re-run for real and passed (marketplace manifest valid). 2.1.259–2.1.263 review (2026-09-06/07): `/skill-doctor`, `bashOutputMaxChars`/`taskOutputMaxChars`, a worktree-isolation permission fix, `/reload-plugins` for headless sessions — see CLAUDE.md's Subagents/Hooks bullets for the full per-item narrative. 2.1.267: the `effort:` frontmatter fix (directly relevant — 27 SKILL.md files here set `effort:`), `maxEffortLevel`, and a marketplace entry-path containment hardening protective of this plugin's `tamirs-marketplace` distribution. 2.1.268: `claude plugin install/uninstall/update/enable/disable --json` — adopted in `scripts/update.sh`/`scripts/uninstall.sh` (see `features_adopted`); `PermissionRequest` hooks firing in `--print` mode; `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSIONEND_HOOKS_TIMEOUT_MS` fix; MCP `${VAR}`-placeholder secret-leak fix; agent-team untrusted-file isolation fix. 2.1.269 (largest delta in the range): a `PreToolUse` deny rule and the `Edit()` write-path check now also apply to a Bash `tee` write, and a `Bash(tee:*)` allow rule is correctly scoped — closes, host-side, exactly the gap `hooks/guard-sensitive-files.sh`'s header comment names and already covers independently via `hooks/lib/write-targets.py`'s own `tee` parsing (neither bug was ever exposed here, since `platforms/claude/settings.d/permissions-allow.json`/`permissions-ask.json` declare no `Bash(tee:*)` rule of either kind); a bare-`!` deny/ask rule leak is fixed (no rule here starts with `!`); the attribution-reminder-overriding-CLAUDE.md bug is fixed (this repo's CLAUDE.md asks *for* the trailer, so never conflicted); plugin-archive extraction hardening (host-side, no manifest change); `claude plugin eval` is genuinely relevant to this toolkit's 27 skills but its `case.yaml`/`prompt.md`+`graders` shape does not match this repo's existing per-skill `evals/evals.json`/`trigger-evals.json` trigger-accuracy harness, so it is tracked as a Future opportunity rather than adopted blind this cycle. 2.1.270: bug-fix-only (a same-week regression in 2.1.269) — read-only git commands in Bash no longer unexpectedly ask for permission after a long-running session; relevant since `permissions-allow.json` pre-allows several git commands specifically to avoid this class of friction. 2.1.271: a stale `.git/config.lock` after a sandboxed command failure no longer breaks `git checkout -b`/`git push -u`/`git config` for the rest of the session (Linux) — relevant since `permissions-allow.json` pre-allows `git push *`/`git remote add *`/`git init` for the same reason, and `hooks/worktree-create.sh` runs through the same sandboxed Bash surface; the Monitor watch deadline change (always at most 30 minutes, 10 in `-p` runs) — `skills/dev-workflow/pr-dev/references/ci-monitor-loop.md`'s one Monitor wrapper already sets `timeout_ms: 1800000` and never set `persistent`, so it was already inside the new ceiling; a background command no longer starting a second copy of itself after compaction, relevant to a long `orchestrate-dev`/`worker-dev` fan-out; cross-session `SendMessage` delivery now gives the headless sender a delivery notice instead of holding the message silently — documented in `docs/user/cross-platform-workflow.md`. `omitClaudeMd` (new agent frontmatter) and per-command `allowed_domains` for auto-mode sandboxing were reviewed and deliberately not adopted: no `agents/*.md` here should skip the target project's own CLAUDE.md, and no shipped rule runs Bash under auto mode with sandboxing. 2.1.272: bug-fixes-and-reliability-improvements only, per the official changelog; no adoptable item. 2.1.273: a 2.1.268 change that checked `Read`/`Edit` deny rules on Bash lines the permission checker cannot fully analyze (`eval`, `env -C`) is reverted — this repo declares no such rule pattern, so the revert changes generic host behavior but nothing this repo declares; `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1` now also tags cost/token metrics with real agent/skill/plugin/MCP-server names — not wired here, this repo ships no OpenTelemetry config of its own; the `New Features` section of the 2.1.273 changelog entry repeats 2.1.271's items verbatim (fast mode in Remote sessions, `/config` mouse support, `--drain-marker-file`, per-command `allowed_domains`, `omitClaudeMd`, `--accept-command <sha256>`, `modelPricing` multiplier) — already reviewed in the 2.1.271 pass above, no new review needed. 2.1.274: a sub-agent's progress summary is no longer replaced by a runaway multi-paragraph reply — directly relevant to `worker-dev`'s `completed`/`partial`/`failed`/`blocked` handoff vocabulary and any `orchestrate-dev` fan-out reading a worker's summary back; `claude agents` no longer loses `--model`/`--effort`/`--permission-mode`/`--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions`/`--agent` after an auto-update — no script here shells out to `claude agents` directly, so not exercised, but relevant to a contributor invoking one of the ten `agents/*.md` from that CLI subcommand by hand; a visible low-memory warning is added (host UI, nothing to adopt); `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_STARTUP_WAIT_MS` is added — reviewed against this plugin's one MCP server (`github`, whose Docker fallback path can be slow to start on a cold pull) and documented as an available knob in CLAUDE.md's MCP bullet rather than set as a repo default, since the right value is workstation-dependent. Reviewed and found not applicable: an `effort` attribute on the OTel span (no OpenTelemetry config shipped here); Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry/telemetry-disabled sessions defaulting to MCP client v2 (this repo targets direct Claude Code/Desktop sessions, not a Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry gateway); a sub-agent `model: "opus"` leaving the wrong session model on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry (all ten `agents/*.md` pin `model: sonnet`, and again no Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry usage); `/code-review` moving to leaner inline prompts (this repo references the official `code-review@claude-plugins-official` marketplace plugin in `platforms/claude/settings.d/plugins.json`, but has it deliberately disabled, so nothing here changes either way). Also reviewed for PR #154/#155/#156/#157 (2026-09-16, merged to master ahead of the prior reconciliation): SessionEnd-hook-budget fix, `handoff-reminder.sh` SessionEnd-schema fix, the 27-skill stale `model: claude-sonnet-4-6` pin fix, and the 3.6.3 release cut — all internal repo fixes with no platform-target, capability, or Claude-Code-host-version impact, so no co-change to the claims above was needed. Tonight's cycle (2026-09-20) had no live `claude` CLI in the automation environment, so this advance from 2.1.274 to 2.1.278 is changelog-only, covering 2.1.275, 2.1.276 and 2.1.277 individually plus 2.1.278: `reviewed_through` and `latest_known` move to 2.1.278 on that basis, same as the 2.1.263→2.1.273 reconciliation cycle did; `validated_against` stays at 2.1.274 — the last version an actual live `claude` CLI run confirmed — rather than being advanced on changelog evidence alone (an earlier draft of this entry made that claim; an automated PR review caught it and it was reverted before merge, see PR #159). 2.1.275: `/plugin install <plugin> --marketplace <source>` can install from a marketplace in one step; reviewed against `docs/user/install/claude-code.md`'s existing two-step `/plugin marketplace add` + `/plugin install` sequence and left as a Future opportunity rather than rewritten this cycle, since the two-step form still works and every existing doc reference assumes it. Skills and plugins enabled on a user's claude.ai account now sync into terminal sessions automatically, opt-out via `syncClaudeAiSkills: false`/`syncClaudeAiPlugins: false` settings — worth a `CLAUDE.md` note (added below) since a user who also has claude.ai skills enabled could see a name collide with one of this plugin's 27 `SKILL.md` names. Plugin/marketplace messages no longer leak a secret embedded in a URL, and `claude plugin marketplace update` no longer deletes the local marketplace copy on a failed fetch — directly relevant to this repo's own `/plugin marketplace update tamirs-marketplace` instruction in CLAUDE.md's Marketplace cache section, since a flaky fetch previously risked wiping the installed cache instead of leaving it untouched; documented there as a reliability improvement, not something requiring a manifest change. A send-now keybinding (ctrl+enter / ctrl+x ctrl+s) is an interactive-terminal convenience with nothing here to adopt. 2.1.276 carried no changelog entry relevant to this repo in the reviewed delta. 2.1.277: Claude Code now reads `AGENTS.md` instead of `CLAUDE.md` when a project has none, configurable under "Project instructions" in `/config` — this repo's own root always ships both (`CLAUDE.md` line 1 is `@AGENTS.md`) and `repo-scaffold`/`multi-agent-repo` always scaffold both files together for any new target repo too, so no project this toolkit touches or generates is ever missing a `CLAUDE.md` for the fallback to engage on; reviewed and recorded as not applicable, not silently skipped. The deprecated `TaskOutput` tool is removed (a breaking change upstream) — grepped every `agents/*.md` `tools:` line and every skill, hook and doc in this repo for `TaskOutput`: zero references, so nothing here ever depended on it. Reliability fixes to `Grep`/`Glob`/`Write`/`Edit`, plugin install/reload, and sandboxed Bash are host-side with nothing here to change. 2.1.278: Auto mode's server-side classifier now defaults on for API/Enterprise/Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry/gateway users (opt-out via `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=0` on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry/gateways) — reviewed and not applicable, same reasoning as every other Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry/gateway item above: this repo targets direct Claude Code/Desktop sessions. No breaking change in the 2.1.275→2.1.278 range affects this repo (`TaskOutput`'s removal is breaking upstream but was never referenced here). See `CLAUDE.md`'s Subagents, Hooks, MCP, Marketplace cache, Skill frontmatter, Claude Code CLI baseline and Remote and headless Claude sessions sections for the per-release narrative in prose form.

codex.supported_min_source: earliest release this repo has claimed AGENTS.md + .codex-plugin manifest support for
codex.verification_method: 0.146.0 was exercised on the maintainer machine; 0.147.0 through 0.152.1 support was reviewed against the official OpenAI release deltas. .codex-version tracks 0.155.1 pending the next direct CLI validation. 0.150 adds native task references and Interrupt hooks; 0.151 adds optional-MCP discovery grace, extension-side MCP result interception, and stronger per-repository plugin catalog handling; 0.152 adds package-style MCP names, per-tool output_token_limit, long app-server shell-command timeouts, and makes update_plan opt-in. 0.152.1 is a Guardian policy fix. None requires a shared plugin-manifest migration. The manifest hooks field is NOT a 0.147.0 feature: 0.147.0 is portable agent plugins (catalog install), while plugin-manifest hooks were wired into the hook runtime by openai/codex PR #19705, merged 2026-04-28, roughly twenty releases earlier. core/capabilities/platforms.json briefly recorded codex hooks as since 0.147.0 on that confusion; the exact floor has never been established here, so the registry now claims none. 2026-09-21 correction (PR #183, objective codex-guard-fix): the same registry row's notes ended with 'Not the same shape as Claude hooks/hooks.json', and docs/user/install/codex.md's capability table said hooks.json 'does not port' to Codex. Both were false and are corrected. hooks/hooks.json DOES port: .codex-plugin/plugin.json points its hooks field at this repo's own file, manifest.rs:149-155 accepts the same HooksFile type the engine consumes, Codex's own test uses plugin_root.join('hooks/hooks.json'), the engine is named ClaudeHooksEngine, it sets CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, exit-2 blocking semantics match, and core/src/tools/hook_names.rs:29-38 ships Claude tool-name matcher aliases deliberately. The narrower true statement is that coverage is PARTIAL: WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove, DirectoryAdded and Notification have no Codex equivalent and never fire. The same table's subagents row (native -> unknown) and MCP row (.codex/config.toml -> the manifest mcpServers field) were corrected in the same pass. All of it is source-derived from openai/codex main; no live codex binary was run, and that caveat travels with the claims. 2026-09-21 review (PR #158): reviewed_through and latest_known advanced 0.152.1 -> 0.155.1 against the official OpenAI release notes for rust-v0.153.0, rust-v0.154.0, rust-v0.155.0 and rust-v0.155.1; 0.155.1 is the newest stable tag, 0.156.0 existing only as alpha prereleases. validated_against stays 0.146.0 - still no live codex binary was run, and that caveat travels with every claim below. None of the three releases requires a shared plugin, skill or manifest schema migration. Relevant to this repo: 0.153.0 gives the plugin CLI remote-marketplace list, install and remove, which is the install path docs/user/install/codex.md documents. 0.154.0 makes existing sessions pick up newly installed plugin tools and refresh skills AND hooks after an out-of-process plugin upgrade or rollback (openai/codex #42284, #42593, #42990) - this matters here because Codex records hook trust per content hash, so a refresh that changes hook content resets it to needing review; the untrusted-by-default gate documented in the install doc still applies after an upgrade. 0.154.0 also removes the deprecated `codex mcp-server` entry point, which this repo never referenced (MCP is declared through the plugin manifest's mcpServers field pointing at ./.mcp.json). 0.154.0 adds experimental native worktree support (--worktree, /worktree) and 0.155.0 adds worktree ownership detail plus confirmed deletion of clean managed worktrees; worktree isolation stays `emulated` in the registry because the skill still runs `git worktree` itself and the native feature is experimental and outside the plugin manifest - adopting it would be a Codex-specific surface, not a shared-hook change. 0.155.0 adds Touch ID user verification for MCP requests in local TUI sessions on supported Macs, and accurate expired-OAuth reporting with reconnect guidance; both are host capabilities needing no manifest change. 0.155.0 also adds configurable daemon update schedules, `codex app-server daemon update`, and saved-thread and active-goal recovery across daemon restarts. Approval and sandbox hardening across 0.154.0-0.155.0: startup no longer runs workspace-controlled PATH helpers before trust is established, the macOS sandbox blocks terminal input injection, Windows process escapes from restricted WSL sandboxes are blocked, and brokered shell snapshots are hardened against credential exposure. 0.155.1 is a single bug fix restoring `none` as the TUI reasoning-summary default for new local sessions (openai/codex #46467), fixing request rejection by providers that do not support reasoning summaries; explicit reasoning-summary settings remain respected.

opencode.verification_method: opencode --version on the maintainer machine (1.18.11), exercised live: opencode debug skill / debug agent / debug config against this repo and against throwaway sandboxes; agent + config field shapes cross-checked against the published JSON Schema at https://opencode.ai/config.json. latest_known from registry.npmjs.org/opencode-ai dist-tags.latest (1.18.29, published 2026-09-04; refreshed 2026-09-08). validated_against is deliberately not latest_known: 1.18.11 is the build actually run, and asserting 1.18.29 would be invention. MCP stays in capabilities because OpenCode reads MCP servers natively, from the 'mcp' block of opencode.json rather than .mcp.json -- but this repo ships no 'mcp' block, and docs/user/install/opencode.md tells the user to port the entries they want. That is a documented path, not a shipped artifact, so it is not the same case as the hooks gap below. core/capabilities/platforms.json validated the claim with jq -e '.mcp // {}' opencode.json, which named a key this repo has never shipped and, because the // {} fallback makes jq -e exit 0 on every input, could not have failed if it had. reviewed_through advances to 1.18.29 on a documentary review of every release from 1.18.12 to 1.18.29 (all 18 tags retrieved individually from the GitHub Releases API; none unverified), supplemented by path-scoped commit history for 2026-08-03..2026-09-05 over src/skill, src/agent, src/config and src/mcp. No breaking change, no $schema or schema-URL change, no change to skill discovery or nesting, no change to agent frontmatter, no change to how MCP servers are declared -- and for skills and MCP that rests on zero commits to the implementing trees in the window, not merely on absence from the release notes. Two things worth carrying forward: 1.18.16 made the config parser ignore unknown top-level fields at runtime although the published schema still sets additionalProperties:false, and 1.18.24 added read-compat for v2 config, whose 'skills' is a flat array rather than this repo's v1 {paths,urls} object -- a future v2 adoption is a real opencode.json shape change even though v1 stays native today. Also confirmed from the loader glob '{agent,agents}/**/*.md' that this repo's singular .opencode/agent/ is supported outright, not merely tolerated. The review is documentary, so validated_against stays at 1.18.11. 2026-09-22 review: reviewed_through and latest_known advanced 1.18.29 -> 1.18.31 against registry.npmjs.org/opencode-ai dist-tags.latest (1.18.31, published 2026-09-14) and commit history for 2026-09-04..2026-09-14 on the upstream GitHub repo, which has moved from sst/opencode to anomalyco/opencode (the npm package name, opencode-ai, and the dist-tags.latest this repo tracks are unaffected; GitHub API requests to the old sst/opencode slug now 301-redirect there). Path-scoped commit history over packages/opencode/src/skill, src/agent, src/config and src/mcp shows zero commits in the 1.18.29->1.18.31 window -- no breaking change, no schema change, no change to skill discovery, agent frontmatter, or MCP server declaration. The published schema at https://opencode.ai/config.json still defines Config.skills as the v1 {paths, urls} object with additionalProperties:false, confirming the v1/v2 divergence already noted above has not resolved either way. Also noted, not yet load-bearing: the same upstream repo carries a separate v2.0.x tag series that does not correspond to any 2.x version of the opencode-ai npm package (no 2.x version exists in that package's version list); unclear what component those tags belong to, and not chased further since it does not affect the npm dist-tag this repo's convention tracks. No live opencode binary was run this cycle, so validated_against stays at 1.18.11.

gemini_cli.verification_method: gemini --version on the maintainer machine (0.55.1); extension format, skill discovery depth, agent validation, and hook config shape measured directly with a probe extension linked into an isolated HOME. Gemini reads skills exactly one level below a skills root, so the canonical two-level skills/<domain>/<name>/ tree resolved to zero; scripts/build-gemini-extension.sh generates a flat symlink mirror at .gemini/skills/ plus translated sub-agents at .gemini/agents/, both committed and drift-checked. Verified live: 30 of 30 skills discovered, all 10 agents load with zero errors. Registry key is gemini_cli (not gemini) so this file, core/capabilities/platforms.json and platforms/gemini/adapter.yaml all name the same platform id. 2026-09-22 review: reviewed_through and latest_known advanced 0.55.1 -> 0.60.0 against the official google-gemini/gemini-cli GitHub Releases for v0.56.0 through v0.60.0 (five stable tags retrieved individually from the Releases API; intervening -nightly and -preview tags were not separately reviewed since only stable tags are tracked here), and against registry.npmjs.org/@google/gemini-cli dist-tags.latest (0.60.0, published 2026-09-15). None of the five releases changes the extension manifest format, the one-level-below-root skill discovery depth, the agent config shape, or the MCP extension path-interpolation this repo depends on -- confirmed by reading each release's PR list, not assumed from silence. Two changes are worth carrying forward as an unverified risk rather than a confirmed break: v0.57.0 (#28867) added a guard that prevents subagents from running when agents mode is disabled, and a related fix (#28882) addressed a sub-agent handoff token regression on startup -- this repo's ten committed .gemini/agents/ adapters were not re-run against either fix this cycle. v0.60.0 (#29169) hardens path resolution and boundary validation in the extension loader, and an adjacent change in the same release window (#28863) expanded the extension-install consent prompt to enumerate a declared MCP server's environment variables and headers (redacting values that look sensitive) -- both land on scripts/build-gemini-extension.sh's generated symlink mirror and .gemini/skills/ output, and neither has been exercised against the current extension since. No live gemini binary was run this cycle, so validated_against stays at 0.55.1.

capability_source_note: targets.<key>.capabilities and capability_gaps are DERIVED from the capability registry and must not be hand-edited. Regenerate with `bash scripts/check-platform-targets.sh . --sync-capabilities`; `scripts/check-feature-equivalence.sh` fails when they drift.
version_claims_note: `validated_against` is the version this repo was last exercised against on a live maintainer machine. `reviewed_through` is the newest upstream release whose notes have actually been read for adapter impact. They are different claims and they drift apart on purpose: reading release notes is cheap and should always be current, while a live run needs a maintainer at a machine. V1-04 fires on `reviewed_through < latest_known` -- nobody has looked at what shipped -- because that is the gap a contributor can actually close. It deliberately does not fire on a validated_against lag, which is bounded instead by `last_reviewed` and V1-05's 90-day budget. A target with no `reviewed_through` falls back to `validated_against`, so consumer repos that have not adopted the field score exactly as before.
